why: The statement asks for finite generation of K-groups of all regular finite-type Z-schemes. Quillen's dimension-≤1 theorem is a classical, journal-of-record case. The in-window Gupta–Krishna–Rathore result proves Kₘ(X) ≅ finite ⊕ uniquely divisible for smooth projective X over finite fields, m ≥ d+1, and so reduces finite generation to D = 0 without proving it for any degree. That is a reduction to an unproven condition, so the answer is none and not case. Hiranouchi–Sugiyama assume the motivic Bass conjecture and do not prove it, so it is also none. The CH₀ result concerns a different group (variant). Stavrova, Balkan–Schreieder, Lehner and Klein–Naef are namesake or neighbouring problems (variant). No AI involvement was found in any event.
doubts: The CH₀ event has no date. It is placed before the snapshot because it rests on Kato–Saito, Colliot-Thélène–Soulé–Sansuc and a 2008 Kerz–Schmidt preprint. Gregory 2023 may contain an unconditional computation of K-groups for a class of surfaces, which would be a pre-snapshot case. It was answered none because a snippet says the main theorem assumes Parshin's conjecture. Either answer leaves the problem open. The acknowledgements of both 2026 preprints were not read, so the finding of no AI involvement is provisional.
